title: Results Manifest
description: Inventory of what a simulation run produced. Emitted by code-generation to the orchestrator, which fans it out to visualization and numerical-analysis. Large data files are referenced by path, never inlined.

numerical_plan_id.description: Omitted for programming-lane tasks, which skip numerical analysis and have no numerical plan to reference.

attempts.description: Chronological journal of the build/run/format fix loop, ALWAYS populated (on success and failure), one entry per iteration. Lets a reader reconstruct how many tries a case took and what each error and fix was, without opening the subagent transcript. The last entry is the outcome this manifest reports; on escalation, escalation.attempts equals this array's length.

error_excerpt.description: Short excerpt of the compiler/runtime/style error that drove the next fix; omit on a passing iteration.

fix.description: The change made in response to this iteration's error.

log_path.description: Per-attempt log, e.g. artifacts/<study-id>/build_attempt_2.log; do not overwrite it across attempts.

command.description: The direct program invocation used for this run, e.g. 'mpiexec -n 4 ./app -pc_type gamg'. Must be the actual executable command (optionally with an MPI launcher), NOT a build-system target such as 'make run' — consumers parse it to recover the executable and its CLI arguments.

convergence_study.description: Present when a refinement study was run.

escalation.description: Present only when code-generation could not reach a passing/usable result on its own and is handing back to the orchestrator. Machine-routable, symmetric with numerical-assessment.recommended_changes. A run that merely converged wrongly is NOT an escalation — return it normally for numerical-analysis to assess.

summary.description: What failed and the supporting evidence.

attempts.description: Number of build/run fix attempts made before escalating; equals the length of the top-level attempts[] journal.

last_error.description: The final persistent error message or symptom.
